thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: continuous-batch latency cliff detected in us-west-2 pool. cont_batch_p95 spiked to ~1.8s at 11:02 UTC, error rate +3%. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/cont-batch/cont-batch-overview

alex: oncall here, paging now. Is this isolated to a single model/pool? tagging @mira @sam

mira: looking — it's concentrated on pool=rbx-gpu-large and correlates with KV cache evictions. Eviction rate jumped at 11:00, prefetch queue length increased.

sam: seeing the same. We have sustained high concurrency from a single customer wave (payments-svc). Microbatch sizes are growing to 48 in the tail. This is causing KV cache thrash and big queuing.

alex: okay, live mitigation plan: 1) reduce max microbatch size; 2) disable prefetch temporarily; 3) throttle ingress for the offending backend. Who can apply the config hotfix?

jordan: I can patch the configmap/feature flags. Suggest reduce CONT_BATCH_MAX_MICROBATCH from 48 -> 12 and enable jitter (CONT_BATCH_JITTER_MS=10). Also flip prefetch_enabled=false for the pool. Doing canary 10% then 100% if stable.

lin: +1. Also recommend setting kv_cache_eviction_threshold lower so it avoids mass evictions: KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.75 -> 0.85? Actually we want to be more conservative (raise threshold) — set to 0.9 to avoid aggressive evictions during burst.

alex: jordan, lin, go for it. mira, sam please validate metrics during rollout. I'll notify SRE and product about customer-impact.

jordan: running patch now (canary 10%):
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch configmap cont-batch-config -p '{"data": {"max_microbatch_size": "12", "jitter_ms": "10", "prefetch_enabled": "false", "kv_evict_threshold": "0.9"}}'
# then rollout to pool selector: pool=rbx-gpu-large, canary=10%
```

jordan: canary rolled to 10% at 11:08 UTC. telemetry stream link: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/streams/cont-batch/4123456789

mira: immediate signal — p95 latency dropped from 1.8s -> 950ms on canary nodes, prefetch backlog reduced. Eviction spikes dropped. Good sign.

sam: applying ingress throttling rule now to shed excess concurrency from payments-svc: set rate_limit=80r/s and concurrency cap to 200 for that service.

ops-bot: deploybot: Canary configmap patch applied by jordan. Change ID: cfg-20260315-041.

alex: customer-impact assessment: payments-svc saw elevated latency and ~2% error rate spike between 11:00-11:12 UTC. A handful of downstream requests retried, but no persistent failure. Notifying account team to surface to customer ops.

mira: broad rollout to 100% at 11:12 UTC after 3m stable canary metrics. Observability: p95 cluster now ~420-700ms depending on model, error rate returning to baseline.

jordan: rolling back previous prefetch aggressive heuristic (we had a transient change earlier this week). Added note to rollout log: revert-heuristic-20260310.

sam: ingress throttle in place, observed rate from payments-svc cut by ~65% within 2m. Queue length on frontends dropped accordingly.

alex: ops-bot — attach runbook entry executed and link to commands. Add timeline.

ops-bot: runbook:cont-batch -> step 3/7 executed by jordan at 11:08 UTC. Step 5 (ingress throttle) executed by sam at 11:10 UTC. Incident state: mitigated.

mira: leaving detailed notes for postmortem: root cause appears to be combined factors: (1) sudden customer concurrency wave, (2) recent prefetch heuristic change that increased speculative prefetch volume, (3) microbatch autoscaling allowed large microbatches under high concurrency that increased memory pressure and triggered KV evictions.

alex: action items (owner):
- revert/patch prefetch heuristic to safe defaults (mira)
- add circuit-breaker on microbatch size scaling (sam)
- improve canary gating on KV eviction metrics (jordan)
- customer outreach + RCA (product)

lin: quick note: we should consider a transient global throttle for pool when eviction rate > X to avoid cascade. Putting a draft proposal in #eng-runtime.

alex: handoff to night oncall @mira at 11:25 UTC — monitoring for regression until 02:00 UTC. I'll update incident ticket and add affected customers list. If p95 climbs above 1.2s we re-open pager.

mira: taking handoff. will watch dashboards and logs, will escalate to infra if evictions rise again.

sam: adding small followup patch — reduce max_microbatch to 8 for next 24h as safety net. Will coordinate a controlled rollout tomorrow with load test.

alex: thanks team. postmortem assigned, will include timeline + customer impact + mitigation playbook. Closing thread but keep it pinned to channel for 24h. :thumbsup:
